quote: As a kaisendon and Kanazawa-oden restaurant, dishes rely on standard (wheat-based) soy sauce and bonito dashi; no gluten-free soy sauce or accommodation is documented.
found: 「市場の海鮮はもちろん、こだわり出汁の金沢おでんや定食、市場ならではの一品料理と美味しい地酒をご用意して皆様のご来店をお待ちいたしております。」
method: 1 plain fetch
note: Cuisine premise (kaisendon + Kanazawa oden + teishoku, dashi-based) is on the page; soy sauce, bonito and allergen handling are NOT — the page never uses the words 醤油 or 出汁の種類. Reword as an explicit assumption or drop 'bonito'.

quote: The menu centers on raw fish and seafood prepared in a shared kitchen; vegans should expect heavy cross-contact with fish and dashi.
found: 「海鮮丼・おでん・定食・朝めし！近江町のうまいもん大集合」「市場の海鮮はもちろん、こだわり出汁の金沢おでんや定食…」
method: 1 plain fetch
note: Seafood-centred menu and dashi are documented; 'shared kitchen' is inference from a single 90-seat restaurant, not a stated fact. Safe as written.

quote: The official Omicho Market listing notes that vegetarian-friendly options are available and the restaurant is child-friendly, with counter seats welcoming solo diners.
found: 「団体様・お子様も大歓迎の全90席！ おひとり様が楽しめるカウンターから10 名以上の団体様のお席までご用意！お子様も安心なメニューや鮮魚が苦手な方も一緒にお楽しみいただけるメニューもご用意いたしております。」
method: 1 plain fetch + Ecosia exact-phrase search 「海鮮つるや」近江町 ベジタリアン
note: LOUD false assurance. The words ベジタリアン/ヴィーガン/vegetarian/vegan appear NOWHERE in the page source (grep: zero hits) and nowhere in search results. The line was mistranslated: 「鮮魚が苦手な方も一緒にお楽しみいただけるメニュー」 means 'dishes for people who are not keen on RAW FISH' — at an oden/teishoku market shop that means cooked meat and simmered items, not plant food. Child-friendly and solo-counter halves are correct; delete the vegetarian half.

why: The only basis for 'limited' was a mistranslation of 「鮮魚が苦手な方も一緒にお楽しみいただけるメニュー」 as vegetarian-friendly; the official listing has no vegetarian/vegan wording at all. Every documented category — 海鮮丼, こだわり出汁の金沢おでん, 定食, 朝めし, 一品料理 — is seafood- or dashi-based, and no plant-only item is documented anywhere. Downgrade to 'no' unless someone obtains a menu.

quote: Bowls are served with miso soup and seafood/nigiri are eaten with soy sauce; no gluten-free soy sauce or wheat-free dashi is documented, so wheat exposure should be assumed.
found: 「※丼には「あおさの味噌汁」が付いてきます。」／「極みにぎり寿司10貫盛 4,300円」「のどぐろ握り」「和牛握り」／和牛ローストビーフ丼: 「口の中でとけるうなぎのタレのようなソースがよく合うローストビーフです。」
method: 1 plain fetch
note: Supported, and the page gives a HARDER piece of evidence than the claim uses: the wagyu roast-beef bowl is dressed with 「うなぎのタレのようなソース」, an eel-tare-style glaze, i.e. an unambiguous soy/mirin wheat source served ON a dish. Soy sauce itself is never named on the page — cite the tare line rather than 'eaten with soy sauce'.

quote: Every dish centers on raw seafood, roe, or meat and bowls come with seafood-dashi miso soup; no vegan items exist on the menu.
found: Full menu is seafood/wagyu: ゆたか最強丼（のど黒、カニ、ウニ、イクラ）, 紅ズワイカニ面丼, のどぐろ丼, ぶりカニ面丼, ゆたか富士山丼（うに、本マグロとろ、和牛）, 和牛ローストビーフ丼, サーモンイクラ丼, 極みにぎり寿司10貫盛; 変更味噌汁 = 名物山盛あら汁／香箱カニ汁／しじみ汁／白子汁; おつまみ = へしこ炙り; お子様限定 = 炙りサーモン、玉子焼.
method: 1 plain fetch
note: 'No vegan items' is fully supported — every listed item, every soup upgrade and both kids' bowls are animal. One over-specification: the standard soup is named 「あおさの味噌汁」 (aosa seaweed), and the page never states its dashi; call it 'miso soup, dashi unstated' rather than 'seafood-dashi'.

quote: Core dishes use flour-thickened curry roux, panko-breaded fried fish, shrimp and pork cutlet, all fried together; no dedicated fryer or gluten-free handling is documented.
found: 「ハントンライスといえば、オムライスに白身魚のフライ・タルタルソースがのった金沢名物グルメですが、こちらでは更に、特大の海老フライが贅沢に2本ものっているんです」／「濃厚でとろみの強い金沢カレーらしさ がありつつ…サックサクの揚げたてカツ との相性も抜群です」／「自家製のデミグラスソース、タルタルソース、カレールーなど、手間を惜しまずに手作りしたメニューで…」
method: 1 plain fetch + official-site fetch for corroboration
note: Solidly supported (article datePublished 2023-07-11, dateModified 2025-06-19). The pork detail is confirmed on the shop's own site — 「スパイスのきいた濃厚ルーに薄めのサクサクロースカツ」 (ロース = pork loin) at https://kanazawa-daidai.com/ — worth adding as a second citation since it is current. 'No dedicated fryer' is accurate as an absence: neither page mentions allergens.

quote: Dishes are built on egg, fish, shrimp, pork and meat-based demi-glace/curry roux; no plant-based preparation is documented.
found: 「オムライスに白身魚のフライ・タルタルソースがのった…更に、特大の海老フライが贅沢に2本ものっている」／「自家製のデミグラスソース、タルタルソース、カレールー」／「サックサクの揚げたてカツ」
method: 1 plain fetch
note: Every element cited is on the page: omelette rice (egg), white-fish fry, two prawn fries, cutlet, tartare (egg) and demi-glace. 'Meat-based' demi-glace is definitional rather than stated, which is fine. Nothing plant-based is mentioned anywhere.

quote: Oden is cooked by simmering ingredients together in a shared dashi broth, so even naturally gluten-free items absorb the wheat-containing soy seasoning and share a common pot — high cross-contamination risk for celiac diners.
found: The cited homepage says nothing about pots, broth or seasoning. The operator's own course page states the OPPOSITE mechanism: 「「おでん懐石コース」は加賀ならではの美しさを「おでん」で表現。食材によって、出汁を変えることにより、常に変化を続ける味わいを楽しめます。」 — the dashi is CHANGED according to the ingredient.
method: plain fetch of homepage + three sub-pages
note: FALSE WARNING on the stated mechanism. This is a kaiseki restaurant that explicitly varies the dashi by ingredient, not a one-pot oden counter, and 「wheat-containing soy seasoning」 is nowhere on the site. The gf 'no' tier still stands on other grounds (no allergen policy, 焼物/肉料理/懐石 seasoning), but this sentence must be rewritten: the shared-pot claim is contradicted by the venue's own copy.

quote: The cuisine is built on Kanazawa oden and Kaga kaiseki seasoning, which relies on soy sauce; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat and no wheat-free alternative is documented.
found: 「伝統的な金沢おでんを現代的な懐石に」／「『懐石』という新しいスタイルの〝金沢おでん〟を提供しています。近江町市場など近郊から直送した新鮮な食材を使って仕立てます。」
method: 1 plain fetch (+ /aboutus/, /course/, /food/ checked)
note: The cuisine half is supported in the venue's own words. The soy-sauce half is not: 醤油 appears on no page of kanazawa-kagami.com. Keep the tier, but label the soy-sauce step as an assumption rather than a sourced fact.

quote: Dishes are based on bonito/kombu dashi and feature seafood throughout the oden and kaiseki courses, so plant-only items would still be cooked in fish-based broth.
found: On /course/: 「おでん懐石コース"金沢" 8,800円 ・季節の前菜 ・白身魚の薄造り ・おまかせおでん 各種 ・焼き物…」, 「おでん懐石コース"かが美" 15,000円 …・おまかせおでん 各種（冬期：カニ面付き）…・肉料理」, 「北陸ならではの「のど黒おでん」もお愉しみいただけます。」 On /food/: 能登天然岩がき／金時草つみれ／刺身盛り合わせ.
method: plain fetch of / then /course/ and /food/
note: Claim is true but cited to the bare homepage, which lists no dishes. Re-point it at /course/ and /food/. Trim 'bonito/kombu' — the site says only 出汁 and never names the fish; the seafood-and-meat-throughout part is what the pages actually prove.

quote: All oden items are simmered together in one shared dashi pot, and the broth and many items (fish cakes, the signature wheat-gluten 車麩) contain wheat/gluten, so cross-contamination is unavoidable.
found: 「車麩。大きなお麩で出汁つゆがたっぷり染み込んでいてジュワジュワ！！やさしい出汁の味をダイレクトに楽しめます！！」／「赤巻。つまりははんぺん。」／「ふかし。蒸したかまぼこらしいですが、モチモチ感のある食感が良いです！！出汁も染みてます！！」
method: 1 plain fetch + official English menu page for corroboration
note: Supported on the items. Two ADDITIONS the claim misses, from the shop's own English menu at https://kachigumi.co.jp/en/ippukuya/ : 'Ebiten 280yen' and 'Goboten 200yen' — tempura, i.e. two more wheat-battered items in the same pot, alongside 'Kurumabu 300yen', 'Chikuwa', 'Akamaki', 'Fukashi', 'Bakudan'. But see the soy-sauce row: the broth itself is NOT documented as containing wheat, so 'the broth … contain[s] wheat' should be dropped from this sentence.

quote: Kanazawa oden dashi is a salt/soy-sauce-seasoned kombu broth; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat.
found: 「まずはつゆから。昆布から取った出汁の塩ベースのスープは昆布の旨みとやさしい塩味の味わいにほっこり美味しいです！！」
method: 1 plain fetch + official menu page (no seasoning info there either)
note: FALSE WARNING. The only person who has actually tasted and described this broth calls it 昆布から取った出汁の塩ベースのスープ — kombu dashi on a SALT base — and never mentions 醤油. The claim asserts soy-sauce seasoning the source contradicts. The real gluten at いっぷくや is solid, not liquid: 車麩, ebiten/goboten tempura and the fish cakes. Rewrite the sentence around those; do not warn a celiac off the broth on evidence that says the opposite.

quote: Plant items (tofu, atsuage, daikon, 車麩) are cooked in the same broth as seafood (bay shellfish, fish cakes) and beef tendon and in a likely fish-based dashi, so they are not free of animal contact.
found: 「金沢おでんを食べてみた(くるまふ、ばい貝、赤巻、ふかし、厚揚げ、牛すじ)」／「バイ貝(梅貝)。大きくてコリコリした食感に貝の旨味が出ていてそこにお出汁。」／「厚揚げ。大きくて出汁つゆをよく吸ってくれて美味しい！」 Tofu and daikon come from the official menu instead: 'Yakidofu(Specially made by Tofuya Shibata) 250yen', 'Atsuage … 300yen', 'Daikon 300yen', 'Konnyaku 200yen', 'Gyusuji kushi 300yen'.
method: plain fetch of blog + plain fetch of official English menu
note: Conclusion stands — 厚揚げ, バイ貝, 牛すじ and the fish cakes demonstrably share one pot. Two fixes: tofu/daikon are evidenced by the official menu, not the blog (add that URL); and 'likely fish-based dashi' is contradicted by the same source, which describes a kombu/salt broth. The animal contact is the shared pot with shellfish and beef tendon, which is enough on its own.

quote: Kanazawa oden is built on soy-and-dashi broth and includes wheat-based items such as 車麩 (wheel-shaped wheat gluten); fried items like karaage are wheat-battered, so shared broth and fryer cross-contact should be assumed.
found: 「金沢おでんは、地元ならではの食材を使ったご当地グルメです。車麩や赤巻きといった特徴的な具材が入り、だしの旨みがしっかり染み込んでいます。金沢ならではの味わいをお楽しみください！」
method: plain fetch + linked menu PDF (pdftotext -enc UTF-8 -nopgbrk)
note: The 車麩 half is confirmed by the venue itself — an unusually clean citation, since the shop names the seitan in its own promo copy. Two corrections: (a) 'soy-and-dashi' — the page says だし only, 醤油 appears nowhere on the site or in the menu PDF; (b) karaage is not on the menu. The venue's actual fried items, from https://sansan.redsun-knzw.com/_pdf/menu.pdf , are 磯辺揚げ and エビマヨ — both wheat-battered, so swap the names in and cite the PDF.

quote: The menu centers on oden and obanzai seasoned with soy sauce and dashi, which in Japan are virtually always wheat-containing; no wheat-free seasoning is documented.
found: 「名物の金沢おでんやおばんざいをはじめ、旬の食材を活かした一品料理が自慢です。」／「車麩や赤巻きといった特徴的な具材が入り、だしの旨みがしっかり染み込んでいます。」
method: plain fetch + menu PDF
note: Menu focus and dashi are supported; soy sauce is not — 醤油 appears nowhere on the site or in the 1 MB menu PDF. Also note 'dashi is virtually always wheat-containing' is wrong as written: dashi is fish/kombu, the wheat is in the shoyu. Reword so the wheat is attributed to the seasoning, and keep the sentence as a stated assumption.

quote: Broths and obanzai are typically made with fish dashi and the menu features karaage, mapo tofu and seafood, so vegetable dishes likely share animal-based broth and preparation surfaces.
found: Menu PDF drink-pairing lines name the food: 「○おすすめのお料理：おでん、おばんざい、青菜炒め、磯辺揚げ」 and 「○おすすめのお料理：麻婆豆腐、エビマヨ、肉みそ豆腐、よだれ鶏肉」.
method: plain fetch + linked menu PDF via pdftotext -enc UTF-8 -nopgbrk
note: 麻婆豆腐 is real but is in the PDF, not the cited homepage; karaage does not exist here — the animal dishes are エビマヨ, 肉みそ豆腐, よだれ鶏肉. Re-cite to the PDF and swap the item names. 'Fish dashi' is inference: the site says だし without naming it. The venue does list 青菜炒め and daily おばんざい, so the vegan 'limited' tier is not disturbed.

quote: All signature items are kabayaki glazed with a soy-and-mirin tare, which contains wheat; there is no documented gluten-free preparation.
found: 「家族５人だけでやっている小さなお店で、・うなぎ蒲焼・どじょう蒲焼・近海物の蟹（ずわい蟹、香箱がに、毛がに）・近海物の海老（甘えび、白がすえび、しまえび など）などを販売しています。」／「【近海物の蟹】加能ガニ（石川県産ずわいがに）や富山新湊産のずわい蟹を店内で茹でて販売しています。」／「近海物の美味しいカニを、天然の塩、浄化水を使って茹でれば当然手間とお金がかかりますし…」
method: 1 plain fetch (+ grep of raw HTML for アレルギー/グルテン: zero hits)
note: FALSE WARNING — 'ALL signature items are kabayaki' is contradicted by the very page cited. Half this shop's business is crab and shrimp, and the page states the crab is boiled 「天然の塩、浄化水を使って」 — natural salt and purified water, nothing else — while the 甘えび/白がすえび/しまえび are sold as fresh seafood. Those are naturally gluten-free. The tare is real but confined to the eel and loach kabayaki, and 'soy-and-mirin' is not stated anywhere on the page. Rewrite to scope the warning to the kabayaki.

quote: The kabayaki tare is a soy-sauce-based glaze made in-house; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat.
found: 「【うなぎ蒲焼・どじょう蒲焼】「うなぎ」も「どじょう」も活きたものを仕入れ、たれ作りも含めすべて店内で作っています。」／「…国産天然のどじょう、活うなぎ、炭、蒲焼タレの材料もこだわれば安くならないのは仕方がないと思っています。」
method: 1 plain fetch
note: In-house tare is documented in the shop's own words; 'soy-sauce-based' is standard for kabayaki but is not stated on the page — mark it as an assumption. Worth adding the practical consequence the page enables: because the tare is made on the premises by a five-person family business, this is a shop that CAN answer 'what is in it', which the record currently forecloses.

quote: The shop deals exclusively in eel, loach, crab, and shrimp grilled on shared charcoal — no vegan items and pervasive animal-product contact.
found: 「・うなぎ蒲焼・どじょう蒲焼・近海物の蟹（ずわい蟹、香箱がに、毛がに）・近海物の海老（甘えび、白がすえび、しまえび など）などを販売しています。」
method: 1 plain fetch
note: 'Exclusively animal, no vegan items' is correct and fully supported. One factual slip: the crab is boiled in-store (「店内で茹でて販売しています」), not grilled — only the eel and loach go on the charcoal (炭). Fix the verb; the vegan 'no' tier is right.

why: This is a retail fishmonger, not a kitchen, and its own listing documents whole crab boiled in nothing but 天然の塩 and 浄化水 plus raw 甘えび/白がすえび/しまえび sold as fresh seafood — naturally gluten-free purchases with no wheat step. The only wheat is the house-made kabayaki tare on the eel and loach, which is a separate product line. 'no' currently warns a celiac away from a counter that sells them plain boiled crab.

quote: Black coffee and espresso are naturally gluten-free and plant-based, so a plain hand-dripped or iced coffee is a low-risk choice here.
found: Review 「淹れたて珈琲が飲める」 (下村さき, 2026/01 訪問): 「近江町市場からひがし茶屋街に歩いて行くとき、寒かったのでおともにコーヒーを…と購入。…ドリップしていれるので、提供には少し時間がかかります。コーヒーだけじゃなく、いろんなドリンク売ってます。」 Second review (2026/07 訪問): 「近江町市場の散策途中に立ち寄るのにぴったりな一軒です。今回はアイスカフェラテをいただきました。」 Page header: 金澤屋珈琲店 近江町市場店 / 喫茶店 / 住所 石川県金沢市十間町27-1 / 営業時間 08:30 - 17:00 / 予算 ～￥999.
http: 200 via s-host desktop URL with iPhone UA (tabelog.com answered directly with the mobile UA); krf.co.jp 200 plain
method: iPhone-UA fetch of the Tabelog detail page + plain fetch of https://www.krf.co.jp/ to confirm the operator
note: Hand-drip is confirmed verbatim by a customer (「ドリップしていれるので…」) and iced/latte drinks by a 2026/07 visit, so the branch is correctly identified (近江町市場店, inside the market) and trading. One caveat: エスプレッソ appears only in Tabelog's 関連のキーワード SEO cloud, not in any menu — either drop 'espresso' or cite it elsewhere. www.krf.co.jp is the operator's own shop site (金澤屋珈琲店オンラインショップ) and confirms the roastery, so it is a valid site link.

why: The record's own positives text says a plain hand-dripped or iced coffee here is a low-risk gluten-free choice, and the Tabelog listing (ジャンル 喫茶店, hand-dripped coffee confirmed by a 2026/01 reviewer, coffee beans sold) shows the core product is exactly that. A gf tier of 'no' contradicts the record's own detail text and warns celiacs off black coffee. 'options' with the caveat that the shop also sells 焼き菓子/ケーキ is the accurate reading.

Plain black drip coffee and iced coffee are documented here and are unambiguously plant-based, so there is nothing for a vegan to ask about before ordering one; 'ask' overstates the uncertainty. 'limited' is the honest tier — a vegan can drink here, but no plant milk is documented, and every reviewer photo is of a dairy latte.
